generation_members.surface_form: The best one-step gradient-boosted tree regression model achieves 165±4 K MAE and 0.89 R² on the test set for melting temperature prediction.
A two-step approach combining unsupervised clustering with supervised regression achieves 156±4 K MAE and 0.92 R², outperforming direct one-step supervised learning.

Tree ensemble methods (gradient-boosted trees and random forest regression) substantially outperform linear models, which achieve MAE >240 K and RMSE >340 K, at least 100 K worse than non-linear approaches.
